mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to concerns about future demand.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over the last quarter signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of quarters following a GDPC1 decline, or the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the last two months signals supply chain disruptions, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face production delays and increased costs.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO drops and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decline for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to concerns about future demand.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% and PAYEMS declines for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint correlation between UNRATE and PAYEMS conditions and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% over the last two months and retail sales (RSAFS) are stagnant or declining, it signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is a major driver of economic growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% in 2 months and RSAFS stagnant/declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint correlation between HOUST and RSAFS conditions and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% over the last three months signals rising inflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the Federal Reserve may tighten monetary policy to combat inflation.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is growing at a rate below 1% annually and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, it signals a potential supply-side constraint combined with tight monetary policy, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy with supply constraints
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint correlation between INDPRO growth and FEDFUNDS conditions and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
